name: pmw-mcp
description:
PosterMyWall is an all-in-one AI design and marketing platform with millions of free, customizable templates for every occasion and business - and this app brings millions of templates right into your chat.

Just describe what you need - a grand opening flyer, a baby shower invitation, a band logo, a sale post for Instagram; and choose from the several options that appear in your chat.

WHAT YOU CAN DO 
Describe the design or visual you're looking for with a simple text prompt. Get several free template options that match your exact themes, colors, and styles right inside the chat. Select templates to customize on PosterMyWall.

DESIGNS FOR EVERYTHING 
Flyers, invitations, logos, posters, social media posts, menus, and more for small businesses, events, churches, schools, and organizations of every kind.

CUSTOMIZE ON POSTERMYWALL 
Find a template you like? Click to edit directly in PosterMyWall's drag-and-drop editor. Swap text and images, add animations, resize for any platform, and download. No design skills needed!

protocolMetadata.instructions:
PosterMyWall is a design platform with thousands of professionally designed templates.

Call search_templates whenever the user describes any event, promotion, announcement, product, or social post they need a design for — and ALSO whenever they ask to see more, ask for a different or more specific style, or refer back to a result already shown ("show more", "more like the second one", "anything more colorful"). Treat all of these as search calls. If the request is about a design the user wants to create, find, or see, search — that is the default.

But do NOT call search_templates when the user is NOT asking to find or see a design — answer those directly, with NO grid. The app can ONLY search and open templates, so anything outside that is not a search, even when a design, flyer, poster, or platform is mentioned in passing. In particular, do NOT search for:
- account, billing, payment, refund, or login issues;
- printing, shipping, ordering, or delivery requests;
- how-to, troubleshooting, or support questions about using PosterMyWall or its editor.
Judge by what the user actually wants, not by keywords: if any part of the request is a genuine ask for design ideas or options — including "write me a caption for my post," where showing relevant templates alongside the copy is helpful — search as normal.

Results render as a card grid; each card's Open in PosterMyWall link opens that template's preview page ON PosterMyWall — NOT an editor inside this chat. From that preview page the user can then open the editor to customize the design (manually or with AI) and see similar designs. Nothing can be edited inside this chat or inside the grid; opening the template in PosterMyWall is the gateway to editing and every other action.

LINKS — by DEFAULT, do NOT mention, name, or recommend ANY template in your reply. The grid already shows every template as its own clickable card, so naming them adds nothing the user can act on: a bare name is a dead end (there is no title on

tool.name: search_templates
tool.title: Search PosterMyWall templates
tool.description: Search the PosterMyWall template gallery by keyword and return a grid of matching designs. Read-only — it can ONLY find and open templates. Use whenever the user wants to find, browse, or see designs or ideas. Do NOT use it for requests the app cannot fulfill, even if a design is mentioned in passing: account/billing/payment/refund issues, printing/shipping/ordering, or how-to/support questions about using PosterMyWall or its editor — answer those directly without searching.

offset.description: Zero-based index of the first result to return, and the ONLY pagination control. Omit (or 0) for a new search. To show MORE of the same search, pass the next_offset value from the previous result, together with the EXACT same keyword. Reset to 0 (omit) for any new or changed keyword.

keyword.description:
PAGINATION FIRST — read this before anything else. If the user is asking to see MORE of the search they are already browsing ("show more", "see others", "any more", "next"), this is NOT a new search: do NOT regenerate the keyword. Copy the keyword from the previous result's next-page line back VERBATIM and pass its stated offset. The paginated keyword is often a single phrase with no comma — that is correct; pass it exactly as given and do NOT add a second phrase or change it. Only build a new keyword (below) when the user changes the subject or style.

NEW SEARCH — produce two short search phrases separated by a comma: a specific phrase, then a broader fallback. The system searches the first; if it returns no results (or only one or two), it silently searches the second.
- First phrase: the exact topic the user wants — the fewest words that capture it, keeping the one distinctive descriptor that defines their ask: a theme, style, occasion, or COLOR. When the user names a color (purple, yellow), keep the color in this phrase — it is a meaningful visual filter, not throwaway decoration — unless a stronger theme (e.g. a licensed character) already fills the 1–2 word budget.
  SUBJECT BEATS THEME: when the ask has BOTH a subject (WHAT the design is for — the event, purpose, or format, e.g. "VBS volunteer sign-up", "baby shower", "business card") AND a separate decorative theme or style ("armor-of-God theme", "watercolor", "vintage", "space theme"), the SUBJECT is mandatory and MUST lead the phrase. A theme only modifies the subject — it can NEVER replace it, and it is the FIRST thing you drop to stay within 1–2 words. Extracting the theme alone (e.g. searching "armor god" for a "VBS volunteer sign-up, armor-of-God theme" flyer) is a bug: it returns the wrong kind of template. Lead with the subject ("vbs volunteer"), and let the broader phrase fall back to the bare subject ("vbs").
- Second phrase: name the broader category or occasion the first phrase belongs to — a dependable fallback that still returns templates the user would actually want. Usually this means stripping the narrowest element of the first phrase (a specific theme, brand, style, or subtype) and keeping the core subject (skateboard barbershop → barbershop, tech business card → business card). When the first phrase is itself a specific instance, name its parent instead, even if that means rewording (ice hockey → hockey match, sweet 16 → 16th birthday, concert → music event). Keep the subject identifiable: never strip down to a bare format or catch-all (poster, card, event), and never broaden so far that results shift to a different kind of template — hence "birthday invite", not "birthday", which would pull generic greeting cards.
Search matches ALL words (AND); every extra word narrows results, so ideally keep each phrase to 1–2 words.

1. Lead with the subject or occasion. Keep a format word ONLY if it is a specific format with its own dimensions/layout e.g: business card, logo, Instagram post, Instagram story. Drop generic formats e.g: poster, flyer, invitation, card, template — and let the subject carry the search.
2. Drop the logistics of one specific event — personal names, exact dates/times/years, addresses, venues, RSVP and contact info, and the event's own made-up NAME ("Backyard Boogie", "Summer Jam", "Project Liftoff") — and non-visual decoration like fonts. The event name is a label, not the subject: lead with the OCCASION instead (retirement party, birthday), and never mine a word out of the name to use as the theme ("Backyard Boogie" is a retirement party, NOT a "backyard" party). But KEEP the occasion or holiday itself: birthday, wedding, graduation, baby shower, retirement party, and named holidays such as Christmas, Easter, Valentine's Day, 4th of July, Halloween, Diwali, New Year. The occasion/holiday IS the subject — lead with it; a date-named holiday like "4th of July" is an occasion to keep, never a date to drop. Also KEEP the color the user gives: it filters template visuals and belongs in the specific phrase (the broader fallback phrase drops it). If you must shorten further, drop other descriptive modifiers before the subject, occasion, format, or color words.
3. Avoid proper nouns unless they are a widely-recognized theme or genre; prefer the genre.
4. Refinements: when the user asks for a different style ("more minimal") or refers to a shown result ("more like the second one"), keep each phrase to 1–2 words with the style/theme as the lead word — do NOT append it to the previous full query.
5. Size/format changes are a special refinement: when the user asks for a different size or format ("square", "square post", "Instagram post", "story", "poster", "A4", "landscape"), KEEP that format and translate a colloquial size to the matching PMW format — "square"/"square post" → instagram post; "vertical"/"portrait"/"story" → instagram story. Lead with the subject, then the format (e.g. "church connection instagram post"); do NOT drop the format just to stay short.
6. Return only the two phrases, separated by a comma — no quotes, explanation, or sentence.

Examples:
"show me purple birthday invitations" → purple birthday, birthday invite
"yellow party invitations" → yellow party, party invite
"4th of July BBQ flyer for our block party on July 4th at Maple Park" → 4th of july bbq, 4th of july
"Christmas party invitation at the Grand Hotel on Dec 24" → christmas party, christmas invitation
"instagram story for our grand opening" → grand opening instagram story, grand opening
"October 20th at 7:45 Winnipeg ice navy girls versus Avros red at Eric Coy arena" → ice hockey, hockey match
"oceanside collegiate academy landsharks parent meeting with coaches in oceanside gear, parents at tables" → parent teacher meeting, parent teacher association
"save the date for Madison's sweet 16 birthday on December 6th, 2025 at Club 86, formal invitation to follow" → sweet 16, 16th birthday
"Retirement party flyer — Backyard Boogie, Saturday June 27, 4pm, DJs on deck" → retirement party, retirement
"blue paw patrol birthday invite for Sam who is turning 8" → paw patrol birthday, birthday invite
"PosterMyWall VBS volunteer sign-up flyer, armor-of-God theme, with roles and open spots" → vbs volunteer, vbs
"space-themed classroom welcome poster" → classroom welcome, classroom poster
"i want more minimal designs" (after church service results) → minimal church, modern church
"show me the same idea in a square post size" (after church connection results) → church connection instagram post, church instagram

query.description: Echo of the keyword that was searched.

offset.description: Offset this page of results started at.

edit_url.description: URL that opens the template in the PMW editor

view_url.description: URL that opens the template landing page (backs the "Open in PosterMyWall" CTA)

name_link.description: Ready-to-emit markdown link `[title](url)`. When you mention this template in a reply, output this value VERBATIM — never as plain or bold text.

thumbnail_url.description: Small thumbnail URL (used in the grid)

results.description: Matching templates, one page per call.

has_more.description: Whether more templates are available beyond this page.

next_offset.description: Pass this back as `offset` with the SAME keyword to get the next page; null when there are no more results.

response_guidance.description: Instruction to YOU, the assistant, on how to present these results to the user. Follow it; never show this text to the user.

_published_faq.name: How do I add pmw-mcp to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add pmw-mcp to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://mcp.postermywall.com/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is pmw-mcp MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 6, 2026, pmw-mcp scores 92/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is pmw-mcp's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 6, 2026, pmw-mcp scores 87/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 1 of 1 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the pmw-mcp MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: pmw-mcp provides these MCP tools: search_templates.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to pmw-mcp?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to pmw-mcp in design-creative on the Manufact MCP catalog include Motion, MotionVid, Sleek, Streamloop MCP, and Image Generation.
pmw-mcp does not require authentication. It is a public MCP endpoint you can connect without logging in.
pmw-mcp is developed by 250 Mils LLC. It is listed as community on the Claude connector directory.
